description: Tech team building hardware-software solutions to monitor astronauts' health in real time using sensors, telemetry, and smart algorithms. We specialize in embedded systems and microcontrollers, and welcome members skilled in biomedical data, UI/UX, or technical docs!
summary:
Our handbuilt smart watch assists cosmonauts' health maintenance on the space mission and after it - in the process of rehabilitation. As many of us know, recovery after space missions is a very rigorous process, and we are looking forward to make it more accessable. 

Much thought, watch is a lot more than just a time management tool. Our model features modern accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetometer sensors, wifi and bluetooth chips, as well as haptic motors, microphones and speakers. Together, they enable our users to keep the rehabilitational process as efficient as possible during and after space missions. 

To enhance our ergonomics, we introduce our website, non-AI bot, and future implementations like social media accounts, specialized app, and many more to keep our project efficient, and, although it's specificity, attractive.
details:
Our first prototype of smart watch primarely focuses on routine maintenance. The sensors check if the austronaut demonstrates an active life style, regularly checks their sleep schedule and maintains their blood pressure.

The impact we look for is to help keep the main source of scientific discoveries safe, making health management a less demanding process.

Our watch is based on ESP32-S3 controller board with custom sensors and chips soldered right onto it. The board is secured by a home printered case, which uses environmentally friendly TPU material.

The code for our watch's operational system is written primarely in C++, and C. It is coded manually by our engineer using Visual Studio Code.

Our project's creativity is to most extent our design. We have our designer and the rest of the team make up the creative ideas for representative presentation slides.

We have always considered the likelihood of unexpected issues. For example, during the coding of the first prototype, we faced lots of challanges like multiple attempts of 3d-modeling our watch's protective case and prolonged code debugging. Considering our pitch, we have spent much time creating the speech to present our innovative solution to juries clearly and cohesively.
